texts.preamble: Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Kabc020170692024 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.2709/2024 Dated this 1st day of December, 2025 Petitioner: Molly Alexander W/o Alexander J., Aged about 56 years, R/at No.FF101, Girija Enclave, Thindlu Bus Stop, Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru North - 560 097. (Sri Shankar Prasad M. B., Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Go Digit Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Consulate 01, 2nd Floor, Richmond Road (near Richmond Circle), Shanthinagar, Ashoknagar, Bengaluru-560 025. (Policy No.D106585130/23062023) (Sri B. Anjaneyalu, Advocate) 2 Mvc No.2709/2024 2. M/s. Bhaghirathi Travel, 2nd Cross, Anekal Road, Kpn Agrahara, Anekal Taluk, Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/ 1 Bengaluru - 560 067. (Ex-parte) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 04-03-2024 at about 7.15 a.m., the petitioner was riding the scooter bearing No.KA-04-JE-2665 on 6th main road of Nagapura ward, from Geleyara Bhalaga towards 11th cross, very carefully, cautiously, by observing traffic rules and regulations. When he was near Sanjeevini Medicals, at that time all of a sudden one school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from the opposite direction of Shankarmath road and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner. Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Prestine Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident she was working as a Technician at Diagnostic Centre and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity. The Rajajinagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of passenger carrying commercial vehicle insurance policy vide No.D106585130/23062023, valid from 23-02-2024 to 23-02-2023 in respect of Tata passenger carrying vehicle bearing No.KA-51-B-0737, in favour of the respondent No.2.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. It has denied the occurrence and mode of the alleged accident and also actionable negligence of the driver of the school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. It has denied that, the alleged Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/ 2 accident is caused by the driver of the insured school bus, but the petitioner herself was negligent and has caused the alleged accident. The petitioner is not entitled to seek for any compensation from the respondents, for her own negligent act in causing the accident. Further it is contended that, the petitioner being the rider of the scooter bearing No.KA-04-JE-2665 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the scooter and she was not wearing safety helmet while riding the scooter and she has violated traffic rules. Further it is contended that, the driver of the insured school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737 was also not holding valid driving licence to drive that class of motor vehicle. The respondent No.2 knowingly and intentionally entrusted the school bus to a person who had no valid driving licence to drive the school bus. Therefore, he has contravened the proviso of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Rules framed there under and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner. Further it is contended that, the bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737 was not having valid permit to ply at the place of accident, as on the date of accident. Further it is contended that, the charge-sheeted driver of the insured school bus has been falsely implanted by suppressing the material facts. by colluding with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the said bus to obtain compensation from the insurance company fraudulently. Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has relied on the following decisions: Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/ 3 i. National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Challa Upendra Rao and others reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517. 8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 57 years is 9. The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge. The said bill has been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,71,360/- towards medical expenses. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,71,360/- under the head of medical expenses. But, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, as on the date of accident the offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 was not having valid permit to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident. Further argued that, as the insured/respondent No.2 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the respondent No.1 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2, for any liability or compensation awarded by this Court. 22. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, there is no breach of any fundamental terms and conditions of the policy, as alleged by the respondent No.1. Further argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a breach of any fundamental condition of the policy, recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the insured.
